newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus party chief gets 15 days' prison for rally.
newsitem.headline: Belarus party chief gets 15 days' prison for rally.

text.p: A senior opposition figure in Belarus has been sentenced to 15 days in prison for organising an unauthorised rally in Minsk earlier this month, a spokeswoman for his Social Democratic Party said on Saturday.
"The leader of our party, Mikola Statkevich, got a 15-day prison term yesterday for the December 8 anti-presidential rally," Lyubov Arestovich told Reuters.
Up to 7,000 people marched in central Minsk to denounce President Alexander Lukashenko and a referendum on November 24 which gave him sweeping powers over rival institutions.
A Council of Europe analysis of the new constitution warned that it fell short of minimum democratic standards.
Arestovich said several people had been sentenced to shorter terms for taking part in the rally last Sunday.

Irma Tabushava, 60, the sister of Justice Minister Valentin Sukala, was sent home from prison on Friday suffering from "serious heart problems" after she was sentenced to 10 days for taking part in the rally, Belapan news agency said on Friday.
Lukashenko has taken a tough line on rallies, banning them during the harvest season. On several occasions police have been sent in to break them up.
Scores of people have been arrested, though most have been held for days rather than months.
Arestovich said 15 people, mostly students, had been fined between $2.50 and $25. The average monthly salary in the former Soviet republic of 10 million is about $50.
"The Social Democrats have started a collection to support victims of political repression in Belarus," Arestovich said. "We would like to collect money to pay lawyers and fines."
The European Union urged Lukashenko on Saturday to restore full respect for democracy and accept a fact-finding mission, warning relations with Europe would suffer otherwise.
